extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary short fiction / students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading of an early-20th-century literary short story (excerpt) focusing on narrative, atmosphere, and credibility of testimony within the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of causation and climax
rubrics_metrics.description: the two presented the most complete possible unity of causation and climax. As a story, beyond which I have no interest, together they are admirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative events and character actions should cohere so that causes lead inevitably to the story's climax; the passage praises the 'most complete possible unity of causation and climax' as an admirable quality in a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of mood (atmosphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: They were enveloped, too, in the consistency of mood loosely called atmosphere; that is, all the details of their surrounding combined to color the attentive mind with morbid shadows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atmosphere is created by cumulative detail — setting, objects, reactions — which together 'color the attentive mind' and sustain a consistent emotional tone (here: morbid/shadowy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility via witness manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Her manner alone put what she related beyond dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony or reported events within the story gain believability from the speaker's demeanor and perceived inability to invent; the narrator notes that McGeorge's conversion rests 'purely on Lizzie Tuoey's evidence' because her manner makes her account seem indisputable.
